sections.subheading: Why reproducibility is built into the design
body: A photochemistry reaction is only as reproducible as your light source, and most LED setups give you no real way to prove what you delivered. LEDi solves both problems at once.

Seven high-power LEDs across four independently controlled color banks, blue, green, red, and white, focus down to a spot roughly half an inch across, small enough for a cuvette or tube and precise enough that specialized lenses do the concentrating for you. A current indicator tracks exactly how much power reached your sample, so you can dial in a condition once and reproduce it exactly on your next run.

An integrated magnetic mixer keeps your sample stirring continuously through the whole exposure, air cooling keeps the LEDs from adding unwanted heat to your reaction, and the head slides along an adjustable rail so you can fine-tune distance from the sample yourself.

sections.title: Multi-Color LED Head and Optical Design
sections.description: Seven LEDs sound like a lot until the real point becomes clear: four completely independent color channels rather than one fixed white output. Blue, green, red, and white each run off their own bank, dialed to exactly the color and intensity a reaction needs without touching the others. From there, specialized optical lenses take that light and focus it down to a spot around half an inch across, tight enough to put real photon density on a small cuvette or tube rather than spreading it thin across open air.

sections.title: Sample Handling, Mixing, and Reproducibility
sections.description: Getting consistent photochemistry results depends on three things staying constant: how the sample mixes, how much light actually reaches it, and how easily both can be repeated.
body: The magnetic mixer runs the whole time a sample is under illumination, not just before or after, keeping concentration even throughout the reaction. Sample format flexibility comes from swappable holders, starting with the standard cuvette holder and moving to tube, vial, or NMR-tube holders as the work calls for it. And because the current indicator shows exactly how much power is reaching the LEDs, one reading noted today reproduces the exact same condition weeks later.
